title: Transcription-factor binding in mammal-conserved promoter DNA predicted gene response to factor knockdown in K562 cells; non-conserved promoter or distal binding had no detectable effect
abstract:
When a transcription factor (TF) was knocked down in human K562 cells, genes with a peak of that TF in mammal-conserved promoter DNA responded more often than expected; peaks in non-conserved promoter DNA, and peaks 10-100 kb from genes, had no detectable effect. This matters because the claim that most of the genome is functional rests mainly on biochemical activity, such as TF binding, in DNA that evolution does not conserve.

We combined CRISPR-interference knockdowns of 150 TFs from a genome-wide Perturb-seq screen with ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks of the same TFs in K562 (2.4 million peaks) and 241-mammal phyloP scores. A peak was conserved if 5 or more of the 101 bases at its summit had phyloP of 2.27 or more, and not conserved if none had. A gene responded if its expression changed with |t| > 3. A linear model with gene and TF fixed effects gave the change in response probability per peak, with 95% bootstrap intervals over TFs.

Binding explained little: genes with a peak within 10 kb responded in 2.5% of cases, and genes with no peak within 100 kb in 2.1%. Conserved promoter peaks (within 1 kb of the transcription start) added 0.15 percentage points (pp) per peak (0.07 to 0.22), more than all 20 placebo fits that gave each TF the peaks of another TF. Non-conserved promoter peaks added 0.03 pp (-0.06 to 0.14). This pre-specified difference was not significant (P = 0.07). It was significant in the strongest third of ChIP signal (0.46 vs 0.04 pp; difference -0.42, -0.66 to -0.15) and for down-regulated genes (0.10 vs -0.05 pp). It was absent in the most highly expressed genes and in peaks outside regions that many TFs bind. At 10-100 kb both classes stayed below about 0.07 pp per peak, so these data cannot tell whether conservation matters for distal binding.

Limits: one cancer cell line; Perturb-seq detects only changes of about 25-70%; most knockdown responses are indirect; a replication with ENCODE bulk knockdowns (44 TFs) detected no effect in any class; several splits were added after the main result. Prediction for a laboratory test: a mutation of the TF motif in a strong non-conserved promoter peak will change expression of the gene less than half as much as the same mutation in a strong conserved peak.

display.caption: Change in the probability that a gene responds to knockdown of a transcription factor, per ChIP-seq peak of that factor, by distance to the gene and conservation of the bound DNA. (a) Perturb-seq, 150 factors; gray ticks are placebo fits with another factor's peaks. (b) ENCODE bulk knockdowns, 44 factors. Bars: 95% bootstrap intervals over factors.
Per-peak effects by ChIP-signal third within each factor. At promoters, only the strongest third of conserved peaks has a detectable effect; strong non-conserved promoter peaks do not.
Conserved (blue) and non-conserved (orange) per-peak effects in all model variants and windows. Asterisks mark analyses added after the main result.
